The ×G metric operates as a probabilistic scoring model that aggregates shot-specific features such as distance, angle, goalkeeper proximity, and shot type into a single continuous variable representing expected goal probability. It leverages machine learning regression to map these features onto a calibrated probability space, where accuracy and reduced bias are achieved through ensemble methods and comparative validation against traditional models. The model's dual nature lies in its ability to function both as a predictive scalar and as a basis for interpretability via SHAP values. Failure modes arise when positional data is noisy or when shot contexts fall outside training distributions. The model’s robustness depends on feature engineering fidelity and generalization capacity across shot archetypes.
